html:
A new public square in Rome built by Julius Caesar next to the old Roman Forum and dedicated in 46 BCE.

The old Forum was crowded, so from 54 BCE Caesar bought up the houses behind it at enormous cost, paid with the loot of the Gallic Wars. The new square was a long courtyard lined with colonnades and shops, with a temple at one end. Caesar had vowed the temple to Venus Genetrix, "Venus the Mother", on the eve of Pharsalus. His family, the Julii, claimed to descend from Venus through Aeneas's son Iulus, the story Virgil later told in the Aeneid. Inside, Caesar set a gilded statue of Cleopatra.

The forum was a monument to one man, not to the Senate or the people. It was finished by Augustus and rebuilt by Trajan. Later emperors copied the idea, and the row of grand squares that followed is called the Imperial Fora. Three columns of the temple stand again today.
sum: A new public square in Rome built by Julius Caesar next to the old Roman Forum and dedicated in 46 BCE.
